clue.text: Polish operatic theme explored by Milton

definitions.meaning: Krzysztof Penderecki, a Polish composer, wrote an opera on the Fall of Man taken from the English epic
John Milton's blank-verse epic of the Fall, published in 1667

explanation.surface: A subject for an opera from Poland that the English poet had already tackled.
explanation.definitionFit: Both senses name the same epic subject: Milton's poem and Penderecki's opera based on it share the title.

clue.text: A clergyman in employment, this novelist

indicators.note: the clergy word sits inside the job word, so in signals one piece placed within the other

parts.note: a post is a job or position of employment
Rev, short for Reverend, is a clergyman's title

explanation.surface: A priest holding down a job turns out to be the very writer in question.
explanation.walkthrough: Fitting, since the Abbé Prévost, author of Manon Lescaut, was himself a clergyman; the leading 'A' only links.
explanation.definitionFit: The Abbé Prévost was the eighteenth-century French writer of Manon Lescaut, so he is a novelist.

clue.text: Yet I don't believe in Buddha — hate him in fact — his temples and his religion" (D. H. Lawrence, letter to Robert Pratt Barlow)

definitions.text: Yet I don't believe in Buddha — hate him in fact — his temples and his religion" (D. H. Lawrence, letter to Robert Pratt Barlow)

parts.words: Yet I don't believe in Buddha — hate him in fact — his temples and his religion" (D. H. Lawrence, letter to Robert Pratt Barlow)
parts.note: a quotation with a word missing before 'temples': the solver supplies Lawrence's contemptuous adjective for the shrines he saw in Ceylon

explanation.surface: A line from a Lawrence letter dismissing Buddhism, with one scornful word left out.
explanation.walkthrough: The printed quotation has a gap after 'his'; Lawrence wrote of Buddha's squalid little temples, and the missing word compares them to a rodent's burrow.
explanation.definitionFit: In the letter the word is an adjective of disgust, likening the temples to a squalid burrow made by vermin.

clue.text: Donalbain as Afro-American landscape artist?

definitions.meaning: in Macbeth, Donalbain is the younger child of the murdered Scottish king, so he is that king's boy
Robert S. ... was a nineteenth-century African-American painter of the Hudson River School

explanation.surface: Could a minor Shakespeare prince be recast as an American painter?
explanation.walkthrough: Read the first sense as a possessive phrase: Duncan's son.
explanation.definitionFit: The painter Robert Duncanson's surname spells out the family relation of Macbeth's Donalbain to King Duncan.

clue.text: Creatures from the pen of Berger, writing in French

definitions.text: Creatures from the pen of Berger, writing in French

parts.words: Creatures from the pen of Berger, writing in French
parts.note: berger is French for shepherd, and a pen is a fold for animals, so these creatures come out of a shepherd's enclosure rather than an author's writing

explanation.surface: Animals that appear in the work of the writer John Berger.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests the English writer John Berger and his pen; read in French, a berger tends flocks in a pen.
explanation.definitionFit: A shepherd's pen holds woolly grazing animals, the creatures a French berger looks after.

clue.text: Renowned little-magazine editor unprofessional, we hear

indicators.note: the clue says the word is heard rather than read, signalling a word that sounds like another

parts.note: a layman is someone without professional training, an amateur

explanation.surface: A celebrated editor of a small literary journal is said to be an amateur.
explanation.definitionFit: John Lehmann edited New Writing and the London Magazine, famous small literary journals.

clue.text: Possibly sit idle, like many TVs

indicators.note: possibly says the letters may be arranged some other way, an anagram signal

explanation.surface: Perhaps lounging around doing nothing, as many television watchers do.
explanation.definitionFit: Flat-screen televisions are often edge-illuminated, with their light coming from the panel's edge.

clue.text: Accomplice on battlefield described by Defoe

parts.note: a moll is a gangster's female companion and accomplice
Flanders, in Belgium, was the scene of great First World War battles

explanation.surface: A partner in crime at the front, as written up by the author of Robinson Crusoe.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue 'on' means placed above, so the accomplice comes first.
explanation.definitionFit: Defoe's 1722 novel tells the life of a thief and adventuress, its title character, so she is the person he portrayed.

clue.text: He spoke for Samuel Butler, in his Way

definitions.text: He spoke for Samuel Butler, in his Way

parts.words: He spoke for Samuel Butler, in his Way
parts.note: the Way is The Way of All Flesh, Butler's novel, whose story is told by a narrator who speaks for the author

explanation.surface: A man who acted as mouthpiece for a Victorian writer, in his own manner.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Way' looks like 'manner', but its capital points to the title of Butler's novel.
explanation.definitionFit: Edward Overton is the narrator of The Way of All Flesh, the voice through which Butler tells the tale.

clue.text: Forster's study of a typically English season?

definitions.meaning: E. M. Forster left an unfinished novel of this title, published after his death
a jokey picture of a British summer as cold as the far north

explanation.surface: E. M. Forster's examination of the usual weather in England.
explanation.definitionFit: The title of Forster's fragment doubles as a gibe at chilly British summers, the polar term qualifying the warm season.

clue.text: Ludwig repeatedly made overtures to her

definitions.text: Ludwig repeatedly made overtures to her

parts.words: Ludwig repeatedly made overtures to her
parts.note: Ludwig is Beethoven, who wrote three overtures named after the heroine of his opera Fidelio, which sounds like a man repeatedly courting a woman

explanation.surface: A man named Ludwig kept trying to woo a woman.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Made overtures' suggests romantic advances; musically, Beethoven composed several overtures bearing the heroine's name.
explanation.definitionFit: Beethoven's Leonora Overtures Nos 1 to 3 take the name of Fidelio's heroine, who disguises herself as a young man.

clue.text: "Myriads of loose white flints in bulbous, cusped, and shapes" (Tess of the D'Urbervilles)

explanation.surface: A description of stony farmland quoted from Hardy, with one word left out.
explanation.definitionFit: Hardy's adjective describes stones shaped like the male organ, a frank touch in his description of the barren field.

clue.text: Mythical flower in violet headdress

indicators.note: in tells the solver that the letters sit within the words that follow

explanation.surface: A legendary bloom tucked into a purple hat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Flower' is crosswordese for a river, something that flows, not a bloom.
explanation.definitionFit: The river of forgetfulness in the Greek underworld is a legendary waterway, and a river is something that flows.

clue.text: Artist showing true iron as a player in The Game of Thrones

definitions.text: Artist showing true iron as a player in The Game of Thrones

parts.words: Artist showing true iron as a player in The Game of Thrones
parts.note: points to the illustrator whose painting of the iron seat of power George R. R. Martin endorsed as the true version from his books

explanation.surface: A painter who proved his mettle by taking part in the fantasy saga.
explanation.walkthrough: 'True iron' suggests strength of character; it means the faithful picture of the Iron Throne.
explanation.definitionFit: Marc Simonetti, a French illustrator, painted the Iron Throne as Martin imagined it, making him a key artist of the saga.

clue.text: Frankau's leader is broadcasting

parts.note: a master is one in charge, a leader
is shortened to 's, as in a contraction
a programme that is broadcasting is on, being transmitted

explanation.surface: Frankau's chief is on the air.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is a single possessive: Gilbert Frankau's novel of 1926.
explanation.definitionFit: Gilbert Frankau, a popular English novelist, published a book with this title, so it is a work belonging to him.

clue.text: Eine Kleine Nachtmusik from Swinnerton and Aiken

definitions.text: Eine Kleine Nachtmusik from Swinnerton and Aiken

parts.words: Eine Kleine Nachtmusik from Swinnerton and Aiken
parts.note: Mozart's title means a little night music; both Frank Swinnerton and Conrad Aiken wrote works named after such evening pieces

explanation.surface: Mozart's serenade as composed by two twentieth-century writers.
explanation.definitionFit: A night piece is music evoking the evening, and both writers used that musical term as a title.

clue.text: Canning's was red, and once contained vinegar

definitions.text: Canning's was red, and once contained vinegar

parts.words: Canning's was red, and once contained vinegar
parts.note: a sacred cup: in George Canning's verse it is red with wine, and at the Crucifixion vinegar was offered to Christ

explanation.surface: Something belonging to the statesman Canning was red and used to hold vinegar.
explanation.definitionFit: A communion cup holds red wine at the altar, a goblet of sacred use.

clue.text: To endure, ode rung differently, (as guerdon perhaps)

indicators.note: differently says these letters are to be put in another order

explanation.surface: Suffering is a poem sung another way, perhaps like a reward.
explanation.walkthrough: The bracket points out that the same letters make guerdon, an old word for reward, as a further anagram.
explanation.definitionFit: To bear or go through something unpleasant is to suffer it, a synonym of enduring.

clue.text: Fairytale monsters uncovered in blog research

indicators.note: uncovered in says the letters are revealed within the phrase that follows

explanation.surface: Storybook beasts exposed by some online investigation.
explanation.definitionFit: Giants that eat people are stock villains of folk tales, the monsters of stories like Jack and the Beanstalk.

clue.text: Once location of highest court made available, by Jove!

definitions.text: Once location of highest court made available, by Jove!

parts.words: Once location of highest court made available, by Jove!
parts.note: the highest court is the gods' assembly once held on a mountain top, and Jove, or Jupiter, presided there; 'by Jove' doubles as an exclamation

explanation.surface: An excited exclamation about the former site of a supreme court being opened up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Highest court' suggests a supreme judicial body; it is the court of the gods, literally high on the mountain.
explanation.definitionFit: The Greek gods' home was a mountain in Thessaly, where Zeus, Jove to the Romans, held court.

clue.text: Nazi thieves of sacred agreement, outplayed by Professor Jones

definitions.text: Nazi thieves of sacred agreement, outplayed by Professor Jones

parts.words: Nazi thieves of sacred agreement, outplayed by Professor Jones
parts.note: the sacred agreement is the Ark of the Covenant, sought by the Nazis in the Indiana Jones film that names them

explanation.surface: German plunderers of a holy pact defeated by an academic.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sacred agreement' stands for the Ark of the Covenant, a covenant being an agreement.
explanation.definitionFit: The Nazis seeking the Lost Ark are plunderers, those who attack and carry off treasure.

clue.text: Always keeps conjunction for culture hero from Arcady

parts.note: ever means always, as in for ever
and is the commonest conjunction

explanation.surface: A legendary founder of Arcadian civilisation forever holds on to a joining word.
explanation.definitionFit: In Roman legend Evander brought the alphabet and laws from Arcadia to Italy, a bringer of civilisation.

clue.text: Copybook, say

explanation.surface: An exercise book used for handwriting practice, for example.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Copybook' looks like a handwriting manual, but split it reads as a copied book.
explanation.definitionFit: A facsimile reproduction of a printed work is a copy, the short informal word for a reproduction.

clue.text: "Souls of poets dead and gone, / What have ye known?" (Keats)

definitions.text: "Souls of poets dead and gone, / What have ye known?" (Keats)

explanation.definitionFit: Keats names the Greek home of the blessed dead, a paradise for heroes and poets.

clue.text: Location of Fermor's main sort of setting

definitions.text: Location of Fermor's main sort of setting

parts.words: Location of Fermor's main sort of setting
parts.note: Patrick Leigh Fermor's travel book Mani describes a region in southern Greece; main sorted gives that name, and the clue asks where it lies

explanation.walkthrough: 'Main sort' hints at the letters of Mani, Fermor's book title, rearranged; the answer is the peninsula containing it.
